chief_complaint: Chronic management of hypertension and COPD with associated metabolic and psychosocial risk factors
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 58‑year‑old woman with long‑standing essential hypertension, chronic obstructive bronchitis, obesity, pre‑diabetes and anemia. She presents most recently with an acute viral pharyngitis on 2012‑12‑19. Hypertension is treated with lisinopril and amlodipine, and COPD is managed with albuterol rescue and fluticasone/salmeterol maintenance inhalers. She receives vitamin B12 injections for a presumed deficiency contributing to her anemia. Socially, she reports a history of intimate partner abuse and limited social contact, and is employed full‑time. A medication review is flagged as due. No recent vital signs, lipid panel, renal function, spirometry, or smoking status are documented.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior medication review flags (2009, 2010), reports of environmental violence, stress, social isolation, unemployment, prior gingivitis episodes (2008‑2009), a previous viral sinusitis (2007), and other historical social circumstances. These indicate past psychosocial stressors that have been addressed, as well as prior dental disease now resolved.

active_medications.name: 60 ACTUAT Fluticasone propionate 0.25 MG/ACTUAT / salmeterol 0.05 MG/ACTUAT Dry Powder Inhaler
active_medications.purpose: Maintenance therapy for chronic obstructive bronchitis

active_medications.name: Vitamin B12 5 MG/ML Injectable Solution
active_medications.purpose: Treatment of B12 deficiency contributing to anemia

social_determinants: History of intimate partner abuse, limited social contact, full‑time employment, risk‑activity involvement, and high school education level; these factors may affect adherence, stress levels, and access to care.
risk_factor_summary: Charlson comorbidity index 2; high clinical complexity; moderate polypharmacy (7 meds). Comorbidity flags: hypertension, COPD, anemia. Cardiovascular risk elevated by hypertension, obesity, pre‑diabetes, and lack of lipid data. Pulmonary risk from chronic obstructive bronchitis with rescue and maintenance inhalers but no spirometry or smoking status recorded. Metabolic risk from obesity and pre‑diabetes (A1c 6.3%). Hematologic risk from chronic anemia with possible B12 deficiency. Potential renal risk (ACE inhibitor use) but eGFR missing. Psychosocial risk from intimate partner abuse and limited social contact. No documented allergies, vaccinations, or mental‑health screening.

Lipid panel absent; ASCVD risk cannot be calculated.
Renal function not available; CKD stage unknown.
Smoking history not documented, critical for COPD and cardiovascular risk.
No pulmonary function test data to stage COPD.
Iron studies, B12, folate, reticulocyte count missing; anemia etiology unclear.
Influenza, pneumococcal, COVID‑19, and shingles vaccination records absent.
No documented depression or anxiety screening despite psychosocial stressors.

clinical_impression: Patient has high‑complexity chronic disease burden (hypertension, COPD, obesity, pre‑diabetes, anemia) managed with appropriate pharmacotherapy but lacks recent objective data (vitals, labs, spirometry, smoking status) to gauge control. Psychosocial stressors and limited social support further increase risk. Recommendations include updating vital signs, lipid panel, renal function, smoking assessment, pulmonary function testing, anemia work‑up, vaccination review, and mental‑health screening.
